title: Show group position to followers who wander off in sessions
summary: In a shared session where only the host can change the passage, a guest who reads a different chapter now sees a bar above the toolbar saying where the group is ("Group is on John 3") with a **Rejoin** button. Everyone can also see who is reading elsewhere and which passage they're on: in the participants list, on faded avatars on the session's tab, and in a participant list that opens right inside the session's tab on desktop. Hosts can press **Ask to come back** on someone reading elsewhere, and that person gets a request with **Not now** and **Rejoin group**.

setup.title: Open the preview on a computer
setup.body: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop, with the browser window at full width. Open the preview link above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like the old Seed Bible, do a hard refresh (**Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac).

setup.title: Get a host and a guest ready, side by side
setup.body: You'll play two people: a **host** who starts the session, and a **guest** who joins. The host must be signed in (Seed Bible emails you a code, so use an inbox you can check). For the guest, use a second browser, or a private/incognito window (**Ctrl+Shift+N** in Chrome or Edge, **Ctrl+Shift+P** in Firefox; **Cmd** instead of **Ctrl** on Mac). Put the two windows side by side, each wide enough that the tabs list shows on the left. Or use two computers.

setup.title: Start a shared session
setup.body: As the host, open **John 3** in a tab, click **Share**, then **Start and share session**. A link is copied to your clipboard. Paste it into the guest's window and open it, doing a hard refresh there once if the page looks old. Check the guest is also on **John 3**.

setup.title: Let only the host change the passage
setup.body: As the host, open the session tab's menu (the **⋮** button on the session's tab in the tabs list) and choose **Session settings**. Under **Navigation**, turn on **Only host can navigate**. The text below it should read "Only the host can change the passage for everyone." Close the settings. Most tests need this; the last section turns it off on purpose.

sections.title: The guest sees where the group is
sections.intro: A guest who reads a different chapter gets a bar on top of the toolbar pointing back to the group.

tests.title: No bar while the guest is with the group
steps: In the guest's window, stay on **John 3** and look at the toolbar at the bottom of the reader.
expected: There is no "Group is on…" bar and no **Rejoin** button.

tests.title: Reading another chapter shows where the group is
steps: As the guest, go to the next chapter (**John 4**) using the chapter arrows or the book and chapter picker.
expected: The guest stays on **John 4** (the host's window stays on **John 3**).
A bar appears along the top of the guest's toolbar reading **Group is on John 3**, with the host's picture beside it and a **Rejoin** button with a curved-arrow icon.
The toolbar's top corners join neatly with the bar, and the bar doesn't cover the last lines of the chapter when you scroll to the bottom.

tests.title: The bar follows the group when the host moves
tests.before: The guest is still on **John 4** from the last test.
steps: As the host, go to **John 5**.
Watch the guest's window.
expected: The guest stays on **John 4**.
The guest's bar changes to **Group is on John 5**.

tests.title: Rejoin takes the guest back to the group
steps: As the guest, click **Rejoin** in the bar.
expected: The guest's window moves to **John 5**, the same chapter as the host.
The bar disappears.

tests.title: No bar flashes while following the host
tests.why: The bar is meant to stay hidden while a host's move is still loading, so it shouldn't flicker on every chapter change.
tests.before: The guest is with the group (on the same chapter as the host).
steps: As the host, go to the next chapter three times in a row, a second or two apart.
Watch the guest's toolbar the whole time.
expected: The guest follows the host to each chapter.
The "Group is on…" bar never appears, not even briefly.

tests.title: The host never sees the bar
steps: As the host, go to any other chapter, for example **Romans 8**.
expected: The host sees no "Group is on…" bar (the guest follows them there as usual).

setup.title: Put the guest somewhere else
setup.body: As the host, go to **John 3**. Wait for the guest to follow, then as the guest go to **Romans 8** on their own. The guest should now see **Group is on John 3**.

tests.title: The guest's avatar on the host's session tab is faded with an arrow
steps: In the host's window, look at the row of avatars on the session's tab in the tabs list.
Hover over the guest's avatar.
expected: The guest's avatar is faded and has a small arrow badge at its corner. The host's own avatar is not faded.
The tooltip shows the guest's name and the passage they're on, starting with **Romans 8** (for example "Romans 8:1–12").

tests.title: The session tab says how many are away
steps: In the host's window, look at the end of the session tab's avatar row.
expected: There's a small toggle reading **1 away** with a down arrow (its tooltip is **Show participants**).

tests.title: Opening the participant list inside the session tab
steps: As the host, click the **1 away** toggle.
expected: A list opens right under the session's tab, titled **Participants · 2**, with an up arrow to close it (tooltip **Hide participants**).
It's split into **With the group · John 3** (the host, shown as "<name> (you)") and **Reading elsewhere** (the guest, with their passage, e.g. "Romans 8:1–12", under their name).
The guest's row has an **Ask to come back** button.
Below the list are **Session settings** and **Share session** links. Each opens the matching window.

tests.title: The guest's own participant list offers Rejoin on their row
steps: In the guest's window, open the session tab's participant list the same way (the toggle at the end of the session tab's avatar row).
expected: The guest's own row ("<name> (you)") is under **Reading elsewhere**, with a **Rejoin** button.
There's no **Ask to come back** button anywhere, and no **Session settings** link (only **Share session**).

tests.title: Open or closed is remembered after a reload
steps: In the host's window, with the list open, reload the page (**F5**, or **Cmd+R** on Mac) and wait for the session to load again.
Click the up arrow to close the list, then reload again.
expected: After the first reload the list is still open.
After closing it and reloading, it's still closed and the toggle shows again at the end of the avatar row.

tests.title: The host's Session settings list shows where people are
steps: As the host, open **Session settings** (from the session tab's **⋮** menu) and look at the **Participants** section.
expected: The guest's row shows their passage (starting with **Romans 8**) and an **Ask to come back** button.

tests.title: Phone width: the participants sheet splits by where people are
steps: In the host's window, make the window narrow like a phone (drag its edge until the layout switches to the phone layout, with the toolbar along the bottom).
Tap the stack of participant avatars in the reader to open **Participants**.
expected: The sheet shows **With the group · John 3** and **Reading elsewhere** headings, with the guest and their passage under **Reading elsewhere** and an **Ask to come back** button on their row.
Widen the window back to full width when done.

tests.title: Phone width: the guest's bar sits above the chapter navigation
steps: Make the guest's window narrow like a phone the same way.
Scroll to the end of the chapter.
expected: The **Group is on John 3** bar sits just above the chapter navigation at the bottom, with a **Rejoin** button.
The end of the chapter isn't hidden behind the bar.
Widen the window back to full width when done.

setup.title: Keep the guest elsewhere
setup.body: The guest should still be on **Romans 8** while the host is on **John 3**. If not, set that up again as in the last section.

tests.title: Asking shows a request to the guest
steps: As the host, open the session tab's participant list and click **Ask to come back** on the guest's row.
Look at the guest's toolbar.
expected: The host's button changes to **Asked** with a check mark and can't be clicked.
The guest's bar grows into a request: the host's picture, **<host's name> asked you to come back**, **The group is reading John 3** below it, and two buttons, **Not now** and **Rejoin group**.

tests.title: Not now hides the request but keeps the guest where they are
steps: As the guest, click **Not now**.
expected: The guest stays on **Romans 8**.
The request goes away and the bar goes back to the plain **Group is on John 3** with **Rejoin**.

tests.title: The host can ask again after 30 seconds
steps: Keep watching the host's **Asked** button for about 30 seconds after you asked.
When it turns back into **Ask to come back**, click it again.
expected: About 30 seconds after the first ask, the button becomes **Ask to come back** again by itself (no reload needed).
Clicking it shows the request to the guest again, even though they chose **Not now** last time.

tests.title: Rejoin group takes the guest back
steps: As the guest, click **Rejoin group** in the request.
expected: The guest moves to **John 3**, the request and bar disappear.
In the host's participant list, the headings go away and both people are listed together; the guest's avatar on the session tab is no longer faded and the "away" count is gone.

tests.title: An old request doesn't pop up later
tests.why: A request that reaches someone who is already with the group is meant to be dropped, not saved for the next time they wander off.
steps: As the guest, go to **Romans 8** again.
Wait 30 seconds after the last ask so the host's button reads **Ask to come back**, then as the host click it.
As the guest, quickly click **Rejoin** or **Rejoin group** to go back to **John 3**.
Now as the guest go to **Romans 9**.
expected: On **Romans 9** the guest sees only the plain **Group is on John 3** bar, not the earlier "asked you to come back" request.

tests.title: Co-hosts can't be asked, and can't wander off
steps: As the host, open **Session settings**, find the guest in **Participants** and choose **Make co-host**. Close the settings.
As the guest (now co-host), go to **Psalm 23**.
expected: The host follows the co-host to **Psalm 23** (co-hosts move the group), so nobody is shown as reading elsewhere.
The guest sees no "Group is on…" bar, and there's no **Ask to come back** button for them.
Afterwards, choose **Remove co-host** for the guest in **Session settings**.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: When everyone can navigate, there's no group bar
steps: As the host, open **Session settings** and turn **Only host can navigate** off. Close the settings.
As the guest, go to **Acts 2**.
expected: The host follows the guest to **Acts 2**, as before this change.
Neither window shows a "Group is on…" bar.

tests.title: Tabs that aren't part of a session look as before
steps: In the host's window, open a new tab that isn't part of the session.
Look at that tab in the tabs list.
expected: It has no avatar row, no participants toggle, and no participant list, and it opens and closes like before.

tests.title: A playing audio note still shows above the nav on phone width
tests.why: On phone width the group bar shares the spot above the chapter navigation with the note sheet shown while audio plays; only one should ever show.
steps: In the guest's window at phone width, with **Only host can navigate** on again and the guest on a different chapter from the host, press the play button above the chapter navigation to listen.
expected: While audio plays, the playing controls show above the chapter navigation and the group bar is hidden; nothing overlaps.
When you stop the audio, the **Group is on…** bar comes back.

notCovered: Two hosts or co-hosts seeing the same 30-second wait on the same guest: this needs three people at once. Unit tests cover the shared wait.
Requests sent by someone who isn't a host being ignored: a guest has no button to send one, so it can't be triggered through the app.
Right-to-left languages (the Rejoin arrow flips), and translated text for the new labels, which is only in English for now.
